modelResponse.episodeSummary: 70-year-old male with ESRD presenting with symptomatic bradycardia and high-degree AV block secondary to life-threatening hyperkalemia.
modelResponse.rhythm: Third-degree (Complete) Heart Block with wide-complex ventricular escape
keyECGEvidence: morphology: AV dissociation; wide QRS escape; tall peaked symmetric T waves; flattened P waves
preEventNote: Progressive PR prolongation then AV dissociation; QRS widening over 20 min
modelResponse.mechanism: Hyperkalemia-induced impaired myocardial conduction and depolarization, leading to progressive AV block and high-degree conduction delay, culminating in symptomatic bradycardia and wide-complex escape rhythms.
contributingFactors: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) with missed dialysis sessions

rejectedAlternatives.why: While possible, the clinical context of missed dialysis and CRITICAL HIGH potassium (7.4 mmol/L) provides a direct, primary metabolic cause.
While the patient has heart failure history, the specific progression of PR prolongation and peaked T waves in the setting of missed dialysis strongly points to electrolyte derangement.

recommendedActions: Immediate emergency management of hyperkalemia (Calcium gluconate/chloride for membrane stabilization)
Intravenous administration of potassium-lowering agents (e.g., insulin with glucose, inhaled beta-agonists, or sodium bicarbonate)
Urgent initiation of dialysis (hemodialysis) as indicated by missed sessions and critical potassium
Continuous ECG monitoring and frequent electrolyte checks
Prepare for immediate transcutaneous pacing if hemodynamics deteriorate further
uncertainty: Specific medication triggers for hyperkalemia are not provided, but the underlying renal failure is the primary driver.
